title: Data Governance for AI
learning_outcomes: Explain data ownership and how it connects to data governance for ai.
Apply data lineage and provenance in the example and predict the output before running it.
Test one realistic edge case for data governance for ai and explain what the example does not prove.

content.intro: This lesson covers data governance for ai through 6 syllabus subtopics preserved from the supplied Generative AI curriculum. Engineer data and context so each request contains the right evidence, at the right level of detail, with access rules and provenance intact.
content.why_it_matters: Data ownership addresses how information is prepared, described, versioned, or governed. Validate the input, keep source and access metadata, handle duplicates and missing values deliberately, and test the downstream effect of a data change rather than treating the data pipeline as invisible plumbing.

items.title: Access and retention policies
items.text: Use access and retention policies as a lens for understanding data governance for ai. Trace its inputs, the operation or decision it describes, the result a learner can observe, and the limitations that matter for the intended task. Confirm the idea with a small example and an explicit check rather than relying on fluent or plausible output.

items.title: Data quality monitoring
items.text: Use data quality monitoring to turn a vague quality claim into an observable criterion. Define a representative dataset, an expected outcome or rubric, a baseline, and the failure categories you will record; interpret aggregate scores alongside examples and affected groups.

items.title: Sensitive-data classification
items.text: Sensitive-data classification is a control problem as much as a model-behavior problem. Establish explicit boundaries in trusted application code, minimize data exposure, test realistic misuse and failure cases, and record who is responsible for reviewing residual risk. A prompt alone is not a security boundary.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet to a local file such as lesson_example.py and run it with Python 3.11+ using `python lesson_example.py`. This is a local/static teaching example; CodeLeaf's current browser iframe previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript and is not a secure Python runner. Do not paste API credentials into the example or public source files.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original snippet and fixed sample inputs, rerun it, then change one input at a time and compare the new output with the stated contract.

content_blocks.title: Provider and version note
content_blocks.text: Model names, API payloads, supported modalities, quotas, pricing, and SDK behavior vary by provider and change over time. Treat linked official documentation as the authority for a live integration; examples here avoid hard-coded production model IDs and secrets.

content.task: Practice data ownership within data governance for ai: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.

summary: Data Governance for AI is one part of a larger generative AI application lifecycle.
Use explicit inputs, criteria, and reproducible examples to test the concept.
Document uncertainty, failure modes, security considerations, and version assumptions.
